claims.title: Sharp matched-pulse memory and acquired retained-device encoded feedback simulator

quoted_fields.interface: Unknown reciprocal linear overdamped thermal RC law, real nonnegative relaxation spectrum allowing arbitrarily many/slow/frozen modes; fixed unknown positive input/output gains; independent Gaussian white detector noise of unknown variance; SUPPLIED initial total-energy bound. Use the matched completed-cell current/observation psi(t)=pi[sin(2pi*t)-2sin(4pi*t)],0<=t<=1, with current/charge zero at boundaries and vanishing moments k=0,1,2. Fresh precommitted response probes preserve the physical law. Later commands obey |u|<=B and precede the current completed observation; policy may depend on full available history and be selected after calibration. Plant and simulator share the SAME finite observation encoding; guard observations are withheld from the controller.
quoted_fields.failure: The pulse changes the admissible physical experiment and suppresses slow directions. No transfer to arbitrary DC,unfiltered voltage,instantaneous feedback or prior interface optima. N1683 m=1 pulse has a2/3 memory floor without invalidating its specialized stability/work guarantees;no improvement of that work optimum is established. Passivity alone is insufficient: weakly damped oscillators break fixed-pulse uniformity. First-moment leakage restores a floor;net-charge leakage destroys the arbitrarily-slow-mode bound. Harmonic-leak tolerance is a supplied calibration condition,not measured hardware or part of the ideal execution. TV controls bounded observed-record events,not unbounded expected work or unobserved state.
